cards.text: The prophet Isaiah opens this message like the LOUDEST alarm clock on earth: 'Awake, awake!' He's calling Jerusalem, the city of God's people, to rise up. She has drunk a cup from the hand of the LORD, and friend, she is NOT doing well.

cards.question: Jerusalem drank from the hand of the LORD the cup of His ___.
Jerusalem took one sip from the cup of the LORD's fury and set it down.

cards.text: She drained that goblet to the dregs, and it's the cup that makes men stagger. So now she's staggering, and she has sons she bore and brought up.

cards.question: Among all the sons Jerusalem brought up, someone is there to take her hand.

cards.text: Then the prophet lists what has hit her in pairs: devastation and destruction, famine and sword. And he asks who will grieve for her, and who can comfort her.
Then the prophet looks at her sons. They lie at the head of every street like an antelope in a net.

cards.question: Jerusalem's sons lie at the head of every street like an antelope in a net. What has happened to them?

answers.text: They have run off to hide

cards.question: The prophet says Jerusalem's fainted sons are full of the wrath of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the prophet says, 'Therefore now hear this, you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine.' Not with wine, friend, but with that cup from the LORD's hand.
Then the prophet passes along what the LORD says, and he calls Him 'your Lord, the LORD, even your God, who defends His people.' Lean in, friend.

cards.question: The LORD who defends His people sees the cup of staggering in Jerusalem's hand. What does He do with it?
The LORD says that from the cup of His fury, Jerusalem will ___ drink again.

cards.text: Never again. But that cup doesn't just vanish into thin air, because the LORD has somewhere else in mind for it.

cards.question: The LORD takes the cup of His fury from Jerusalem. Whose hands does He place it in?
What did Jerusalem's tormentors tell her?

answers.text: Lie down so we can walk over you
Bow down to our gods every day
Leave this city and never return

cards.text: So she made her back like the ground, like a street for them to walk on. I think this one hurts, friend.

That wake-up call again, friend, 'Awake, awake,' and there's no snooze button on this one. This time the prophet calls Jerusalem Zion and the holy city, and he tells her to clothe herself with strength.

cards.question: Strength isn't the only thing the prophet tells Jerusalem to put on. What else?
The prophet says the uncircumcised and unclean will keep coming into Jerusalem, the holy city.

cards.text: Then: 'Shake off your dust! Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem.' Friend, I wore a whole COAT of dust in that junk drawer for years, and nobody ever told me to go sit on a throne.

cards.question: The prophet calls Jerusalem the captive Daughter of Zion. What does he tell her to remove from her neck?

cards.text: Then the LORD says she was sold for nothing. NOTHING, friend, and I went for 25 cents at a bakery closing sale thinking I was the bargain of the century.

cards.question: The LORD says Jerusalem was sold for nothing. How does He say she will be redeemed?

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD looks back at His people's past, one place at a time.

cards.question: At first God's people went down to ___ to live, then Assyria oppressed them without cause.

cards.text: And now? The LORD says His people have been taken without cause, and those who rule them taunt. On top of that, He says His name is blasphemed continually all day long.

cards.question: The LORD says that on that day, His people will know that He is the One who speaks.

cards.text: And then the LORD says it plainly: 'Here I am!' Three words, friend, so let them sit a minute.
Now the prophet turns our eyes to the mountains, where messengers come bringing good news, peace and salvation. And he has something to say about their feet.

cards.question: The prophet says the feet of those who bring good news are beautiful.

cards.text: Beautiful FEET, friend, and in all my years hopping around on this gold base, nobody has EVER called it beautiful. And these messengers have a message for Zion.

cards.question: The messengers on the mountains bring good news. What do they say to Zion?

cards.text: Then Zion's watchmen lift up their voices, and they shout for joy together.

cards.question: Why are Zion's watchmen shouting for joy?

cards.text: Then the prophet tells the ruins of Jerusalem to break forth in joy and sing together. Ruins that SING, friend, and that's not a city getting back on its feet, that's a city getting back on its feet and doing a little dance.

cards.question: The ruins of Jerusalem break forth in joy, for the LORD has ___ His people.

cards.text: Then the prophet says the LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations.

cards.question: The LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations. What will all the ends of the earth see?

answers.text: The fall of their own kings

cards.text: Then a new call: 'Depart, depart, go out from there!' Believe me, friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I know what it's like to hear that it's finally time to get out.

cards.question: The prophet calls out, 'Depart, depart, go out from there!' Who does he tell to go out and purify themselves?

answers.text: Those who carry the vessels of the LORD
Those who guard the city walls
Those who rebuild the city ruins

cards.text: Then the prophet tells the ones carrying the LORD's vessels how this exit is going to go.

cards.question: The prophet says those who carry the vessels of the LORD will leave in a hurry and flee in haste.

cards.text: No running out the door with one shoe on. The prophet says the LORD goes before them.

cards.question: The LORD goes before those who carry His vessels as they leave. Who is their rear guard?
